answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post bids, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud or duplicate control. A zephyr-like burst of accounts therefore cannot gain influence for free: each one ties up capital, and a glacier of fake identities makes the attacker’s exposure grow roughly with the number of accounts. Honest agents can keep stakes small through clean history, while yarrow-style random audits make evasion uncertain.
